drg.description: Simple Pneumonia and Pleurisy without CC/MCC

timeline.text: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity
Transthoracic echo: LVEF 59%, grade I diastolic dysfunction

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 82-year-old male admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.42, bnp 188, creatinine 0.78, hemoglobin 13.2, platelets 197, sodium 139, wbc 7.9; vitals dbp 70-75, heart_rate 79-83, map 86-89, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 118-121, spo2 97-98, temp 36.8-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Furosemide 20 mg PO daily (home med); Transthoracic echo: LVEF 59%, grade I diastolic dysfunction
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.79, hemoglobin 13.2, platelets 193, sodium 139, wbc 8.3; vitals dbp 71-75, heart_rate 78-83, map 89-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 120-125, spo2 97-99, temp 36.8-37.1
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Furosemide 20 mg PO daily (home med)
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 82-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
